pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: SIMPLE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the role of sentences in a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify simple sentences from varied texts
2. construct simple sentences on a variety of issues

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: SIMPLE SENTENCES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: SIMPLE SENTENCES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify simple sentences from varied texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify simple sentences from varied texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify simple sentences from varied texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify simple sentences from varied texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct simple sentences on a variety of issues

What this means
In this part you learn to construct simple sentences on a variety of issues. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct simple sentences on a variety of issues.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct simple sentences on a variety of issues. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify simple sentences from varied texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences to a partner. (skill: construct simple sentences on a variety of issues)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify simple sentences from varied texts.
3. Practise this skill: construct simple sentences on a variety of issues.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the role of sentences in a text?
2. What constitutes a simple sentence?
3. How do you determine what to include in a sentence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify simple sentences from varied texts.
5. Be able to: construct simple sentences on a variety of issues.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
